mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover together, commuting traffic expands weekday passing trade and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism is falsified if retail does not improve after a two-week rise in both series.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise relative to their current weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A continued increase in RESIDENTIAL time signals stay-at-home substitution that suppresses discretionary shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above its recent weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT below the recent range indicates weaker access to commercial areas, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points below its t-1w mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -35.4 at t-1w and -29.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior four-week average after TRANSIT crosses the stated threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS stays above baseline and rises on warm-weather weeks, leisure time shifts toward outdoor recreation instead of indoor shopping, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days despite PARKS remaining above zero and near its recent highs.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain depressed while RESIDENTIAL is elevated, a restriction-like mobility regime is active and retail visits fall over the next four weeks because trip chaining and commuting demand stay weak.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stay at least 30 points below baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays above 5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days even though the low-work, low-transit, high-residential regime persists.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL implies more local errand bundling and less discretionary shopping substitution, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL are not falling.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM from its recent trough signals restoration of everyday neighborhood activity, which feeds through to broader shopping trips and raises RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises at least 3 points above its t-1w value
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -30.0 at t-1w to -26.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its last-four-week mean after GROCERY_PHARM crosses the stated rebound threshold.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS stays elevated while TRANSIT remains weak, summer leisure substitutes for downtown shopping and the combined effect pushes RETAIL_REC down over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying above baseline and TRANSIT remaining below baseline.
